extracted.intended_audience: people contributing code, documentation, or proofs to the mathlib (Lean) repository
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, and getting reviewed pull requests (code, lemmas, documentation, and style changes) to the mathlib (Lean) repository, including workflow, review process, labeling, and community expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss your contribution on Zulip
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Zulip to discuss your contribution before and while you are working on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a GitHub account and add your GitHub username to your Zulip profile using the personal settings panel. Strongly encourage setting your display name on Zulip to be your real name. Starting discussion on Zulip helps get feedback early and find reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the style guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the style guide for contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRs fixing style violations documented in the style guide are welcome. Other stylistic PRs that don't have explicit approval by the authors of the affected files may be closed; instead discuss on Zulip and seek consensus, and when significant consensus is reached open a PR to the style guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the project's naming conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the naming conventions documentation linked from the contribution guide. Naming conventions affect maintainability and integration with the rest of the library; discuss if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow documentation guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the documentation guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation should follow the documented standards for style and content; use the documentation guidelines linked from the contribution guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer small fixes and single-lemma PRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Small fixes (e.g., fixes in docstrings) and single-lemma additions in already-existing theories are almost always welcome; longer PRs that extend existing theories are also almost always welcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller, self-contained PRs are easier and faster to review. For new contributors, smaller PRs prevent wasted effort and speed feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate whether new theories fit mathlib
rubrics_metrics.description: Before adding completely new theories, consider whether the material is a good fit for mathlib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: Is the material typically taught or studied in a mathematics department? Would it naturally be part of an undergraduate/graduate course or research-level study group? Is the topic within the mathematical interests of the mathlib maintainers? The remit is not 'all of mathematics and related areas' — if unsure, discuss on the #mathlib Zulip channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider who will review your PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Think about who is going to review your potential PR; contributors are encouraged to seek out reviewers for their PRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PR reviewer does not have to be a maintainer; reviews from new reviewers are welcome. If your contribution is outside maintainers' expertise, it may be harder to maintain and review — consider a standalone repo instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider creating a standalone repository when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the area does not align with maintainers' expertise, consider a standalone repository and add mathlib as a dependency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standalone repositories are good for projects that want to move quickly or are outside maintainers' interests. Many Lean repositories are indexed by 'reservoir' and examples exist (e.g., combinatorial game theory repository).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on AI use for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Using an LLM when writing comments on GitHub or Zulip is not allowed: use your own words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use LLMs to write comments on community platforms; comments must be written by the contributor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on AI-assisted code generation
rubrics_metrics.description: AI tools may be used to generate code but raise concerns and have expectations around disclosure and human supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use AI (e.g., GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Gemini, Aristotle), explain this in the PR description: which tool(s) you used and how. You must be able to vouch for all code submitted and understand the content written by an AI. Code written by an AI without the supervision of a Lean subject expert currently fails to meet mathlib's standards; low-quality PRs produced using LLMs may be summarily closed without comment. Repeatedly opening such PRs without demonstrated learning effort may lead to suspension or permanent ban from opening PRs and from Zulip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master branch policy: master must compile and have no 'sorry's
rubrics_metrics.description: The master branch is the 'production' version of mathlib and everything in master must compile without errors and there must be no 'sorry's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only commit changes to master that have passed automated CI tests and have been approved by mathlib maintainers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work on a branch in your fork
rubrics_metrics.description: While working on a new contribution, do so on a different branch in your own fork of the mathlib repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical workflow: fork mathlib4 on GitHub, clone your fork locally, create a new branch (git switch -c my_new_branch), make changes, commit (git commit -a), optionally compile locally with lake build, run lake exe mk_all if you created new files, then push and open a PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build and CI expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: You may compile locally (lake build) to check you didn't break anything, but it's okay to rely on central CI servers; continuous integration will run on your PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View CI status on the PR page (green tick / yellow circle / red cross) or using the GitHub CLI (gh pr status). After CI finishes, run lake exe cache get to download compiled oleans. If CI fails, address issues before expecting merge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make PRs small and self-contained when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: If you've made a lot of changes, try to split into many PRs containing small, self-contained pieces; smaller is generally better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps get feedback as you go and makes review easier and faster, especially for new contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow commit message conventions and include Moves/Deletions
rubrics_metrics.description: The title and description of the PR should follow commit conventions. If moving or deleting declarations, include Moves: and Deletions: lines at the bottom of the commit message before '---'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other comments you want to keep out of the PR commit body should go below the '---' separator. Use the provided format for Moves and Deletions to aid reviewers and automation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make your PR appear on the review queue (use labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many reviewers use the review queue to identify PRs ready for review; ensure your PR appears on that queue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check if your PR is on the queue and, if not, what is needed to get it on. The review queue is controlled by GitHub labels; add or remove labels on the PR (if you have collaborator rights) or use comment commands listed in the guide to change labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label commands and common labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels can be added/removed by writing specific commands in PR comments (each on its own line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'awaiting-author' / '-awaiting-author', 'awaiting-zulip' / '-awaiting-zulip', 'WIP' / '-WIP', 'easy' / '-easy', 'help-wanted' / '-help-wanted', 'please-adopt' / '-please-adopt'. Topic labels t-* (e.g., t-topology), and labels CI and IMO also exist. See available topic labels for a full list. This list is exhaustive; propose new labels on Zulip if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and guidance for the 'easy' label
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'easy' label should mark PRs that can be immediately approved; maintainers and reviewers often look at easy PRs first to keep the queue flowing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical easy PRs add a single lemma, correct typos in documentation, or similar. A PR is generally not easy if the diff is more than 25 lines, it changes any existing definitions or theorem statements, it adds any definitions or new files, or it adds any simp lemmas or instances that are not immediately analogous to existing ones. Small diff alone does not automatically make a PR easy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of other labels (WIP, RFC, awaiting-CI, blocked-by-other-PR, delegated, merge-conflict, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various labels indicate PR status: WIP, RFC, awaiting-CI, blocked-by-other-PR, delegated, merge-conflict, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIP indicates foundational work still needed (e.g., contains 'sorry's). RFC indicates potentially controversial PRs needing expert decision. awaiting-CI hides PR from main review queue while CI runs; auto-removed when CI completes. blocked-by-other-PR is for PRs that depend on others; add dependent PR numbers in a comment to trigger the label. delegated means a maintainer delegated final merging; merge-conflict is added automatically when conflicts exist and removes PR from the review queue until fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can review and who can merge
rubrics_metrics.description: There are different reviewer groups: anyone, reviewers, and maintainers. Maintainers have final approval and merge rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone can review; reviews from non-maintainers are welcome and considered. If a reviewer thinks a PR is ready, they might leave an 'approving' review and add 'maintainer-merge' to prioritize it. Maintainers give final approval and may merge PRs; availability affects review times.

rubrics_metrics.name: What happens after maintainer approval (bors/merge queue)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a maintainer has approved your PR, a 'ready-to-merge' label is automatically applied and a bot called bors will add the PR to the merge queue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The merge queue is processed automatically (building branches of mathlib); processing can take time. If a maintainer delegates the PR (label 'delegated'), the author should merge themselves once final changes are made and CI succeeded by commenting 'bors merge'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with merge conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: When your PR conflicts with changes on master, a bot will add the 'merge-conflict' label and your PR will not appear on the review queue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve merge conflicts (e.g., using GitHub's online tool). Once resolved, the 'merge-conflict' label is automatically removed and the PR returns to the review queue. See the linked GitHub tutorial for conflict resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rebase or squash after review activity (merge, don't rebase)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathlib PRs are squashed upon merge; once a PR has seen some review activity, it is strongly recommended not to rebase or squash anymore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebasing/squashing after reviews obfuscates the review history and makes further review harder. If you don't know what rebasing is, you may skip this section, but avoid rebasing after significant review activity.
